line: e4 c6 d4 d5 f3 Nd7 e5 c5
teaches: A pawn chain is attacked at its base, not at its head. The front pawn is defended by the one behind it, so hitting the rear pawn is the move that asks a real question — take the base away and everything in front of it is loose.
explains: With the pawns locked on d5 and e5, the white centre rests on d4, and the pawn arriving on c5 hits exactly that square. The head of the chain on e5 cannot be attacked profitably while it is defended from behind, so play goes after the pawn holding it up instead.

line: e4 c6 d4 d5 f3 Nd7 e5 c5 c3
teaches: When the base of your chain is attacked, add a pawn defender before you add a piece one. A pawn holds the square without being driven off, while a piece tied to defence has to keep standing there and can be chased.
explains: Before this the base on d4 was held only by the queen, which is a defender you would rather not commit so early. The modest pawn move gives d4 a second guard that nothing can harass, so the centre holds and the pieces stay free to develop where they want to go.
